titel: How to Expose a Genocide: The George Washington Williams Story

einzeiler: The extraordinary life of George Washington Williams, who exposed the Congo genocide.
kurzfassung: George Washington Williams was a pioneering 19th-century soldier, politician, and historian who became the first to coin the concept of crimes against humanity. After initially being deceived by King Leopold II, Williams traveled to the Congo and documented horrific atrocities and forced labor. His courageous open letter sparked an international pressure campaign that eventually ended Leopold's brutal colonial rule.
stichpunkte: George Washington Williams is credited with coining the concept of crimes against humanity during the late 19th century.
King Leopold II of Belgium established the Congo Free State, extracting immense wealth through rubber and resource exploitation.
Leopold used deceptive tactics and PR narratives to convince global figures, including Williams, that his project was a benevolent Christian mission.
Williams had a turbulent and remarkable early life, fighting in the U.S. Civil War at age 14 and later becoming the first Black state legislator in Ohio.
He authored a groundbreaking two-volume history of Black Americans in 1882, earning praise from scholars like W.E.B. Du Bois.
Upon visiting the Congo in 1890, Williams witnessed widespread forced labor, mutilation, and extreme violence against the native population.
He published a meticulous open letter to King Leopold detailing 12 points of horrific abuses, igniting a transatlantic information war.
Williams contracted tuberculosis and died in England at age 41, unaware that his advocacy would eventually force Leopold to relinquish control of the Congo.

clips.text: King Leopold II held personal ownership over a vast territory in Central Africa containing immense natural riches like rubber, which was becoming crucial for manufacturing tires and electrical wires.

clips.hook: A rapid rise in politics and law
clips.text: Williams achieved numerous historic milestones in the 1870s and 1880s, including graduating as the first Black student from a theological institution, starting a newspaper, studying law, and winning election to the Ohio legislature.
Williams broke new ground by writing the first comprehensive history of Black people in America at a time when prevailing racist views claimed Black people had no history at all.

clips.hook: Formal accusations of crimes against humanity
clips.text: Williams sent formal letters to government officials accusing the Congo Free State of participating in the slave trade and committing numerous crimes against humanity.

beschreibung:
Do you ever feel powerless in the face of an atrocity? Well, that never stopped George Washington Williams, a Black man who went from being a “barely literate” veteran to a crusader who exposed a genocide in the Congo and nearly toppled a king. Garrison and activist Mohammed Elnaiem discuss how we can learn from someone who let his faith and love for Black people around the world guide his actions.
